Description -
Position Overview
The Vice President, Agentic AI Systems & Solution Engineering reports into PS engineering leadership and is accountable for common Agentic AI systems architecture, engineering execution and product delivery. The role leads a global, matrixed engineering organization from requirements and system design through development, integration, validation, production release and sustaining.
Working with division leaders and Product Management, this leader converts customer priorities into technical requirements, a prioritized roadmap and executable delivery commitments. Division leaders and PM own customer, portfolio, product and commercial decisions. The VP owns engineering feasibility, architecture, resources, schedule, quality and delivery, with shared accountability for customer adoption and business impact.

Solution Ownership and Deliverables
Own engineering delivery across four connected solution areas, using shared architecture and agreed interfaces with HP platform, security and product teams.

•   Agentic distribution. Own trusted compute discovery, device-capability and model-compatibility checks and authorized task handoff across devices. Deliver distributed execution services, runtime integration APIs and deployable packages supporting continuity, progress visibility and return of results.

Key Responsibilities
Engineering Execution and Product Delivery
•   Own the integrated engineering plan from concept through production and sustaining. Establish deliverables, named owners, milestones, capacity, critical dependencies and release criteria for each committed product or solution.
•   Translate PM-aligned customer needs into functional requirements, engineering specifications, architecture and prioritized development backlogs. Agree scope and acceptance criteria with product owners, and manage changes against delivery commitments.
•   Run a disciplined delivery cadence with engineering, program management and validation leaders. Track progress against evidence, resolve blockers, escalate decisions early and execute recovery plans when scope, schedule, cost or quality is at risk

Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.

At Ping Identity, we believe in making digital experiences both secure and seamless for all users, without compromise. We call this digital freedom. And it's not just something we provide our customers. It's something that inspires our company. People don't come here to join a culture that's built on digital freedom. They come to cultivate it.

Our intelligent, cloud identity platform lets people shop, work, bank, and interact wherever and however they want. Without friction. Without fear.

While protecting digital identities is at the core of our technology, protecting individual identities is at the core of our culture.  We champion every identity. One of our core values, Respect Individuality, reminds us to celebrate differences so you are empowered to bring your authentic self to work.

We're headquartered in Denver, Colorado and we have offices and employees around the globe. We serve the largest, most demanding enterprises worldwide, including more than half of the Fortune 100. ### **Location: US, Remote (Eastern Hours)**

### **About BOI**

BOI is the AI partner that Walmart, Coca-Cola, and Mastercard call when AI needs to drive growth, not just savings. We rebuild how work gets done, starting from the outcomes each team exists to deliver: agents do the work, people own the judgment, and the capacity it frees goes to growth. We bring together the unusually strong in frontier enterprise AI, then give them the ownership to make it happen. If you're looking for a comfortable place to hide, we're not it. If you want to build the future of enterprise AI with people who will make you better: welcome home.

### **Your Role**

### **Own the Technical Build**

* Own the architecture and engineering quality of every client build, from first prototype to production in the client's environment.
* Shape solution architecture across models, clouds and platforms, and make build, buy or configure calls you can defend to a client CTO. Our clients run on Azure, AWS and Google Cloud. We're independent of every vendor, so the answer is whatever is best for the client.
* Set the engineering standards every build meets: evaluation of AI outputs, security and data governance, observability, and production reliability.
* Build the reusable components, patterns and internal products that let each engagement start further ahead than the last.

### **Lead with Clients**

* Sit with client CTOs, CIOs and business executives as BOI's senior technical voice. Explain technical choices in terms of cost, risk and value, so non-technical leaders can decide.
* Lead client security, compliance and procurement reviews, and get our systems approved to run in their environments.
* Work forward deployed: get into client environments early, build alongside their teams, and keep building as the relationship grows.

### **Shape What We Sell**

* Scope and estimate builds for proposals with our Directors of Applied AI, so what we sell can be built on time and to standard.
* Turn what we've built into case studies, reusable IP and technical thought leadership.

### **Build the Team**

* Lead, coach and grow our engineering team, roughly doubling it over the next year. Set high standards, give direct feedback, and give credit generously.
* Run AI-first ways of working across engineering, with your own tools and workflows as the example.
* Help build BOI like an owner, alongside our leadership team in the US and Europe.

* You've shipped AI systems to production at enterprise scale, inside environments with real security, compliance and data constraints.

The Homeland Sector operates across some of the world's most consequential transportation, security, infrastructure and government missions.

Its portfolio spans air traffic management, airports and borders, security screening, energy and critical infrastructure, and substantial businesses in the United States, United Kingdom and Australia. Across these markets, customers are modernizing long-lived operational systems while adopting software, data, AI and other rapidly evolving technologies.

Technology must therefore do more than support individual programs. It must help shape where Homeland competes, how it grows, what it invests in and how it improves execution.

THE 4 BIGGEST BLOCKCHAIN STRENGTHS ARE ALSO ITS WEAKNESS

 - Permissionless nature leads to fragmentation of meaning

 - Decentralization leads to too many standards https://xkcd.com/927/

 - Immutability leads to exponential data + query infrastructure complexity

 - Neutrality means that no one is accountable for interpretations

Blockchain data is public. It is not usable at institutional scale. Despite being open, blockchain data is fragmented, hard to interpret, and painful to maintain. Even a simple question like “Who are the largest Ethereum token holders over time?” can require running nodes, ingesting full chain history, decoding contracts, cleaning edge cases, and writing complex SQL.




BLOCKCHAINS ARE OPTIMIZED FOR WRITES, NOT READS. 

They are built for consensus and execution, not searchability, standardization, or financial interpretation. Blockchains are computers, not databases https://x.com/Tim_Roughgarden/status/1512847113599729668. Every protocol defines its own schema. The same economic action can be encoded in dozens of different ways. The result:

 - Fragmented standards

 - Exponential complexity

 - No accountability for interpretation

 - Events without economic meaning

Finance cannot operate on that, it needs an effective system of record.




ALLIUM IS BUILDING THE SYSTEM OF RECORD FOR ONCHAIN FINANCE

Allium ingests, verifies, and standardizes data across 140+ blockchains and 30+ petabytes of history. We close four structural gaps that prevent blockchains from becoming systems of record:

 - Semantic Gap: Translating raw events into financial concepts like payments, trades, deposits, and staking income

 - Standardization Gap: Mapping thousands of protocols into a single canonical cross chain schema

 - Infrastructure Gap: Read optimized, globally distributed data at web scale

 - Accountability Gap: Auditable methodology, SLAs, and SOC 1 and 2 compliance

The result is a neutral, canonical data layer institutions can build on with confidence.




FINANCE IS MOVING ONCHAIN

Stablecoins, tokenized assets, trading, staking, and lending are growing rapidly. Institutions need a trusted source of truth for onchain financial activity, just as they rely on Bloomberg or DTCC in traditional markets. Raw blockchains cannot serve that role.

As AI agents begin transacting autonomously https://x.com/AlliumLabs/status/2019810793324482901?s=20, the requirement becomes even stricter. Agents cannot reason over raw event logs. They need structured data, attribution, condition checks, and auditability. 

Allium is the read layer that makes onchain finance usable for humans and machines.

Over the last 10+ years, Ellevation Education has built a thriving business serving the administrators, teachers, and specialists who support English Learners. Today, nearly 2,000 school districts use our software to manage their EL programs. We are a successful, growing business with a real mission: helping English Learners achieve their highest aspirations.
Districts across the country rely on Ellevation for the daily workflows that keep those programs running and the student data behind every instructional decision, and we earn that trust through what we build. We’re building a platform that is secure by design and fast to work on, and engineering practices that let eight squads ship with confidence. Much of that is still unbuilt. We want leaders who study how we work today, find the gaps we haven’t seen yet, and then design and build the systems, practices, and team that close them.
Ellevation operates as part of Curriculum Associates (“CA”) which provides several shared functions across all of its business units, including a centralized security organization. Ellevation runs its own R&D organization including engineering, product, and design; CA supplies scanning, security tooling, reporting, and KPIs.
Ellevation R&D spans engineering, product, and design, organized into eight product squads. Each squad owns its product area end to end and moves quickly within it. The work that spans squads, such as platform modernization, authentication, dependency currency, and security, needs deliberate ownership to move at the same pace.
 
 

About The Role
This is a senior role in R&D, and its impact reaches everything Ellevation builds. You’ll see across all eight squads, spot the problems and opportunities that sit where their work meets, and make a case for which of them matter most to the business. Platform modernization, authentication, dependency health, and security are where that work starts today, and you’ll shape what comes next.

You’ll lead a team of Staff Engineers who drive critical parts of this work, making the case for where their time goes and making sure every initiative has a clear owner, a plan the squads can work with, and an agreed outcome. We expect to grow the team over time, and you’ll shape and lead that hiring.

Your impact scales through your team. Our Staff Engineers work across squads, partnering with engineering managers and product leads to move shared work forward within real squad capacity. You'll help them choose the right problems, sequence work across the organization, and grow as technical leaders. You'll stay close enough to the technical detail to judge tradeoffs and stand behind your team's decisions.

Security is a core part of this portfolio, and we want a leader with meaningful security experience to own it. You'll lead security practice at Ellevation, working with CA on the standards, SLAs, and KPIs we're measured against and making sure Ellevation meets them. You'll also be a key liaison to CA's central sec

ABOUT POSH

We are all social creatures, but the dominant “social” companies today have evolved into digital loneliness machines, driving isolation, anxiety, and mental health challenges around the world.

Human connection is lost. Posh is a beacon guiding us back.

Posh enables anyone to build an IRL community based on shared interests, while connecting consumers with the communities of people just like them. Founded by event organizers who were frustrated with the growing loneliness epidemic and the tools available to build their own event brand, we’ve built the ultimate platform for launching, monetizing, and finding IRL communities of people just like you. In just 6 years, Posh has grown to a team of 70, expanded to 10M+ users, secured $70m in venture funding, and facilitated over $400M in transactions.





ABOUT THE ROLE

As our Head of Data and ML, you will own the entire data function. You’ll be accountable for the technical excellence and vision of the team that builds event discovery for 1M MAUs, the experimentation and measurement that guide product investment, and the data platform the whole company relies on to make decisions.

This is a rare opportunity to lead a unified data organization, providing clear direction and impact across the business. You’ll lead a talented multi-disciplinary team of 8 data scientists, machine learning engineers, and analytics/data engineers. Your job is to keep the team’s bar and vision sharp as Posh scales: choosing the right problems, making sound decisions, and shipping work that moves the product forward.

Your day-to-day will involve:

 - Balancing team leadership with hands-on technical work as a true player-coach

 - Translating a product-oriented vision into a technical roadmap the team believes in

 - Working hands-on in analysis reviews, experiment critiques, model evaluations, and building prototypes yourself when it moves things forward

 - Mentoring senior ICs into leaders and helping mid-level ICs level up

 - Setting a culture of rigor, urgency, and craft across every discipline on the team

This role is in-person 5 days a week at our SoHo, NYC headquarters. Relocation bonuses are available for out-of-state candidates.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN

 - Be the technical translation layer: Turn the product vision into focused data and ML bets, and give the team the context to make good calls on their own. When product brings you an idea, you sharpen or debate it, say what’s possible, what it will cost, and what we’ll learn. When something isn’t possible yet, you can explain why and lay out the path to get there. Own the data narrative at All Hands, leadership reviews, and board updates.

 - Build Posh’s discovery and search systems: Advise the team as they build our ranking, recommendation, classification, and search algorithms, from problem framing and baselines to offline evaluation and online testing. Define the metrics that prove discovery is getting better every quarter.

 - Make experimentation

Who We Are Looking For
Are you a hands-on engineer who would rather build automation than manage a roadmap? We're hiring a Process Automation Engineer to design and support automated business workflows. This is a maker's role. You'll write code, wire up integrations, and turn manual processes into automation that holds up in a regulated environment.
The role sits within Process Engineering & Automation at State Street Investment Management (formerly State Street Global Advisors). Day to day, you'll work with the Process Automation Lead, business architecture, business units, and technology teams to turn process designs into working software. We're moving toward a Product, Platform, and Service operating model. AI and agentic automation are part of the toolkit, but so are boring, reliable things like scheduled jobs, process models and well-tested APIs. Your job is to pick the right tool for the problem, build it well, and make sure it doesn't page anyone at 3am. No hype-driven adoption. Practical automation that runs in production without drama.

Key Responsibilities
- Build the automation. Design, build, test, and support automated business workflows in Appian (or whatever replaces it). This is where you spend most of your time. You're hands-on, in the code, every week.
- Fix broken processes. Work with business architecture and business units to take manual, high-friction workflows and turn process designs into software that runs. Sometimes the process design is clean. Sometimes you'll push back on it because it won't survive contact with real systems.
- Own your delivery end to end. Carry your work requirements through deployment and support. What you ship meets enterprise standards for security, resilience, controls, and maintainability. Regulated environment, no shortcuts.
- Connect systems. Build integrations between the orchestration platform and the systems around it. Clean APIs, sensible contracts, nothing held together with duct tape.
- Test and support what you build. Write the tests, fix the defects, and stay close to your solutions in production. Instrument processes so operations can see where things get stuck before users file a ticket.
- Try new tools. AI, agentic automation, whatever shows up next. Pilot what looks promising, be honest about what doesn't work yet, share what you learn with the team.
- Work across pods. We operate in a matrix model with cross-functional pods spanning product, platform, and service lines. You'll embed with different pods depending on the work, collaborating with product owners, platform engineers, and service teams who know the business domain. Your job is to bring automation engineering, not sit in a silo waiting for requirements to land in your lap.
- Raise the bar. Follow the team's delivery controls and engineering standards. Help improve them. If something's slowing everyone down, say so and propose a fix.

As a member of the CTO's leadership team, this leader will define and drive a new operating system for how the company builds software, set engineering-wide standards for tools and processes, and lead the use of artificial intelligence to transform software engineering and deliver more value for our customers.

We serve institutions and their students, all of whom are navigating how artificial intelligence changes teaching and learning. As Director of Product Architecture, you will be the senior technical authority for authorization-related products across our product portfolio. - Experience shipping enterprise security or identity products at scale.
- A track record of driving alignment across multiple teams without direct authority.
- Exposure to AI agent security, non-human identity, or API and gateway enforcement is a strong plus.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to explain complex architecture to executives, customers, and engineers alike.

Success looks like
- A single, well-understood authorization architecture adopted across the product teams.

Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. The Senior Director, AI Enablement owns the production of role-specific AI capability: the Skills, projects, agents, product education and workflows that make GPS, Prism and our data platform usable inside the job, for the roles that matter most. Alta Resource Technologies (Alta) is a next generation mining company that uses synthetic biology to separate critical minerals from conventional and unconventional resources, including e-waste. Founded in 2023, the company is expanding its team in Boulder, CO. The exponential growth of new tech industries, as well as the information technology sector, are driving historic growth in mineral demand and stressing existing supply streams. Meeting new demand, diversifying the supply chain, and producing minerals in a more sustainable manner requires the rapid development, deployment and scaling of new technologies. This mineral challenge represents a historic opportunity for technology development and value creation. Alta is proud to be at the vanguard of this mega trend.

About the Role

Alta is seeking a Head of Data Science and Automation to own the data and automation backbone behind our research, development, and scale-up. This is a hands-on, player/coach role at the Director level: you will build and run the systems while hiring, leading, and developing a small team of data and automation engineers.

You will own the data pipelines, laboratory information management (LIMS), Ignition, and the integration of laboratory instruments and process equipment, so that every sample, run, and result across our design-build-test-scale cycle is captured, traceable, and ready for analysis and modeling. Our computational biology team relies on this data to build and refine predictive models, and you will partner closely with R&D, Engineering, and the build, test, and scale teams.

We measure this role by its impact on the business: faster design-build-test-learn cycles, higher throughput, data people can trust, and better decisions that move candidates toward commercialization. You will join a collaborative group of scientists and engineers with diverse skill sets, and bring strong communication, critical thinking, and a rigorous, practical approach to problem solving.

Key Responsibilities
- Build and maintain version-controlled, well-documented data pipelines that bring data from instruments, LIMS, sequencing, and process equipment into a central data platform.
- Establish data models, metadata standards, and ontologies so data is findable, linked, and reusable, enabling genotype-to-phenotype tracking across the full workflow.
- Deliver analysis-ready datasets to the computational biology team and define with them the data their models need.
- Implement data quality monitoring, validation, and provenance tracking so results can be trusted and reproduced.
- Provide statistical analysis, experimental design support, and dashboards that help teams make faster, better decisions.
- Select, configure, administer, and extend Alta’s LIMS/ELN and sample management systems, including barcoding, chain of custody, and sample genealogy from design and construct through testing and production lots.
- Integrate LIMS with instruments, liquid handlers, and downs

About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Hardware Engineering to lead the team that designs and builds our robots. Mechanical, electrical, firmware and embedded, and manufacturing engineering all report to this role. You set the hardware roadmap with the CTO, you grow the team, and you are responsible for every robot we ship working as designed and building at the rate we need. You report to the CTO.
The hardware organization will grow a lot, in people and in the range of products it covers. The person in this role builds the teams that make that happen, hires the people who lead them, and keeps the whole thing running well as it gets bigger.

- You have led and grown a hardware engineering organization to 50 or more people, and shipped a complex electromechanical product in volume through it
- You have led mechanical, electrical, and firmware or embedded engineers, and can hire and judge all three
- You have owned manufacturing engineering, or worked closely enough with it to build that team: process, test, fixtures, and design for manufacturing
- You have developed the managers who lead teams under you
- You have worked closely with a technical founder or CTO
Nice to haves

Enterprises do not buy AI infrastructure one product at a time. They buy it from the reseller who already holds the paper, the services capacity, and the trust. Your first targets are the partners where our path to the money is right now: WWT and Computacenter, then SHI, CDW, and the national and regional VARs that actually sell AI infrastructure. You can pull in distributors, and the OEM and ISV partners your peers own, where they accelerate a deal; the global system integrators (Accenture, Deloitte, EY) stay with the VP.

This is a founding, zero-to-one role on a first-year partner program. NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology—and amazing people. Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIAN, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.

NVIDIA’s advanced datacenter boards push forward chip packaging, PCB fabrication, SMT, assembly, and testing capabilities. Dedicated teams take responsibility for each technology: packaging manages the package, PCB and materials handle fabrication and stack-up, SMT and assembly oversee build processes, and test and SI focus on test capabilities. The challenge is to align these improvements across the stack—from chip to PCB, PCB to SMT, SMT to assembly, and assembly to test. Each domain’s innovation delivers maximum benefit when downstream consequences are considered early. The Senior Director, Board PDE oversees integration methods that make this possible—coordinating handoffs, engineering cross-domain effects before changes, and optimizing the entire chain.

What you'll be doing:
- Design, implement, and institutionalize the integration readiness process for all next-generation datacenter board products — owning manufacturing and test readiness end to end so build starts land on schedule and at target yield.
- Guide the functional teams in developing cross-boundary techniques before silicon and stackup freeze occurs. Focus on warpage-tolerant DFM and reflow for next-gen BGA pitch. Manage impedance and CTE control for high-speed stackups. Lock pad-map and fab methods at an early stage.
- Build, lead, and develop a global Board PDE organization across three technical pillars — PCB & Fab, SMT/PCBA, and High-Speed Connector & Signal Integrity.
- Set up integration oversight throughout the chip-to-board stack. Define entry and exit requirements at each domain boundary. Lead the gates to confirm one qualified domain is ready to pass to the next.
- Collaborate with Operations Test Engineering and Signal Integrity to establish test coverage and manufacturing test flow requirements, applying that thoroughness to the tester and diagnostic boards.
- Take charge of reliability and yield performance throughout the stack. Investigate excursions to identify root causes. Address DFx and alternate-component gaps with the factory planning and design teams.
- Support manufacturing partners (CM/ODM/OSAT, substrate, and PCB fab) in producing world-class datacenter products. Serve as the senior chip-to-board representative across NVIDIA's Operations, Engineering, and Executive teams.
